title: KV fragmentation / compaction benchmark results (mixed-length burst + churn workloads)
content:
metric_definitions:
frag_ratio_* is allocator-reported KV arena fragmentation ratio (0.0 = fully contiguous free space, 1.0 = maximally fragmented free space) sampled at prefill/decode boundaries; compaction_cpu_ms_per_s is wall time spent in compaction worker per 1s of benchmark time (host-side orchestration + device copies as reported by runtime timers); bytes_moved_gb is total KV bytes relocated by compaction over the run; evictions_per_min counts sequence KV evictions (tier-aware LRU) caused by allocator pressure (not user cancels); throughput_tok_s is aggregate decode throughput across all replicas in the run; p50/p95/p99_ms are end-to-end request latencies (prefill+decode) at steady state window (excluding warmup).

environment:
Benchmark lab cluster (isolated), CUDA 12.4, NCCL 2.20.x; H100 runs use HGX H100 80GB nodes; A100 runs use A100 80GB SXM nodes; L4 runs use GCP L4 24GB; driver versions pinned per lab image; all runs executed with identical workload seeds unless otherwise noted in notes.

highlights:
Across H100/A100, incremental compaction (2ms / 256MB budget) reduces frag_ratio_end from ~0.7–0.9 to ~0.2–0.4 in churny mixed-length workloads with ~1–2% throughput cost.
Tail latency improvements are consistent in burst scenarios: p99 reductions ~25–40% (largest when baseline shows allocation retry spikes).
Background compaction keeps fragmentation lowest but introduces periodic p95 micro-spikes; scheduler-budgeted incremental mode is the preferred default.
Under near-OOM pressure on A100, compaction alone is not always sufficient; tier-aware eviction prevents OOMs at the cost of elevated p50/p95 during eviction windows.
High-cancel workloads surfaced a relocation/cancel race; fixed in redwood/pr-19440 and validated (KVF-0047).

open_questions:
Should Dedicated default budgets be slightly higher than Hosted (e.g., 2ms/256MB vs 2ms/192MB) given steadier load and stronger tolerance for small throughput hit?
What is the maximum acceptable eviction rate before user-visible quality/UX issues (especially for long multi-turn chats)? Need product guidance + customer evals.
Do we want model-specific compaction thresholds (frag trigger) to account for KV page size differences across architectures?

notes:
This sheet is maintained as a lightweight, PR-friendly export for review in runtime/SRE threads. Runs tagged mixed_len_burst_churn_v3 use the benchmark-lab workload generator introduced in benchmark-lab/pr-881. Unless specified otherwise, each run includes 120s warmup, then steady-state window sampling for p50/p95/p99 and fragmentation snapshots. For comparisons, focus on paired runs with identical seeds and concurrency. Any run with tracing enabled should not be used to set throughput regress thresholds; it exists to validate correlation and exemplar selection for dashboards.
